teaser: Not no backend: no tech stack of your own. Only HTML, CSS and JavaScript; every other primitive rented or run in the browser over vaults.
core_idea: An application over sgit vaults still has a backend, but every part of it is a commodity: a static host, an encrypted file store, and when needed a model provider or agent platform. The only code you maintain is the HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The usual primitives remain: immutable data cached for ever, a database compiled to WebAssembly in the browser, passkeys with the PRF extension for users with no server-side user data, append lanes for messages, PKI for sharing between users, and models in the browser or behind a host that holds the key. The constraint pushes simpler designs and leaves the server holding only ciphertext; the gap is a clean way to give keys to the client.
